brief: The author held no strong directional bias but expected a tricky September/October followed by a strong November/December; after this week's reading he lands with slightly more conviction that risk favors the bulls. Kevin Warsh's FOMC delivered a hawkish surprise, killing one-and-done hike hopes, yet financial conditions eased afterward: the back end settled, breakevens tightened, equity vol compressed, and long-duration stocks outperformed, leaving today's setup better than a month ago. GS's house view (Dom Wilson) is that the Fed underdelivers versus four hikes priced, more likely two. Because price drives sentiment, the author notes S&P is tracking a fourth straight double-digit year with improved breadth, yet positioning surveys are downbeat and PB net exposure sits at the 34th percentile, a contrarian bullish setup. Counterweights: rising energy prices against falling inventories, an unresolved Iran tail risk, and the compounding squeeze of higher gas prices and 7% mortgages on a consumption-heavy economy, prompting core equity length paired with commodity trading length and options on higher rates. He expects S&P higher at year-end, with equities, rates, and commodities trending higher, earnings decelerating but not collapsing, and gold's $5,400 target intact as Fed hikes slow, not kill, the rally.
